newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Zalakeramia Q1 profits up, exports down.
newsitem.headline: Zalakeramia Q1 profits up, exports down.

text.p: Hungarian tile manufacturer Zalakeramia Rt on Tuesday reported higher profits for the first quarter of the year on rising domestic sales but declining exports.
"Exports in the first quarter were 27 percent below exports for the same period of last year," the company said in its earnings report.
Zalakeramia reported an IAS net profit of 144.2 million forints for the first three months of 1997, up from a net profit of 105.4 million in January-March 1996.
Operating profits grew to 156.3 million forints from 114.3 million on what the company said was a successful refurbishment of its Romhany plant.
Overall sales grew to 1.028 billion forints from 743.9 million as higher domestic sales offset falling exports.
The company's exports declined to 120.7 million forints, down from 164.4 million in the first three months of 1996.
"The decline occurred generally in all our (export) markets...," Zalakeramia said. "The market of the product is characterised by big supply, very depressed prices and fierce competition."

Zalakeramia added that an expected recovery has not materialised in either the company's traditional German and Austrian markets or its new Romanian, Slovenian and Commonwealth of Independent States markets.
The company which earlier this year acquired a 78.3 percent stake in Croatia's Inker ceramics manufacturer, is building strong export hopes on that market.
"Sales to the Croatian market began in the second quarter of the year and it is proving to be a substantial export market in terms of pace (of growth) and volumes," Zalakeramia said.

On the Hungarian market, meanwhile, Zalakeramia reported a 56.7 percent increase in sales, to 908.0 million forints in the first quarter of 1997 from 579.5 million in the first quarter of 1996, with a rise particularly in freeze-proof tiles.
